notes: D-006 correction, not oracle parity. An entry name that is itself an absolute path (leading '/') bypasses the target directory entirely once handed to a shell unzip's -d argument resolution the same way a ../ traversal does, just without needing any relative segments -- it's a distinct case from zip-slip-relative-traversal-rejected because a naive traversal-only check (rejecting only entries containing '..') would miss it. MSC 1's unzip -o call (line 718-719) has no defense against this. Phase 6's extractor must reject any entry whose path is not a plain relative path confined to the target root -- an absolute entry path is refused outright, same all-or-nothing archive-level refusal as the relative-traversal case.
